newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall St's bullishness surges across Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall St's bullishness surges across Atlantic.

text.p: European bourses ended higher on Friday but off their best levels for the day after Wall Street burst higher in early trade only to shy away from its highs.
European markets were swept higher in early trade when the impact of Wall Street's dramatic two percent rise on Thursday surged across the Atlantic.
The Dow vindicated the market's optimism by rising more than 70 points within the first 15 minutes of trading on Friday but then had second thoughts and ceded some of its gains.
"The Dow carried us up and it carried us back down," said one London share dealer.
U.S. blue chips were up about 25 points after Europe's market's had closed.
"The Dow's jump overnight was unbelievable," one senior dealer in London said earlier in the day. "It certainly has given the market a boost of confidence."
Europe's major bond markets edged higher too, lifted by Thursday's strong bond rally in the United States, lending further support to stockmarkets.
British shares ended up, but well off their record peaks set earlier after an early burst of buying on Wall Street faded, dealers said.
Surging U.S. stocks propelled the benchmark FTSE 100 to an intrdaday record at 4,100 briefly before slowly giving back gains. The index ended 26.3 points higher at 4,077.6.
Today's advance added another leg to the UK market's long-awaited year-end rally, usually attributed to seasonal inflows of cash into investment fund coffers.

And with a recent spate of takeover bids promising to inject further cash into the market, as well as prompting further gains in other possible bid targets, some traders and analysts said the FTSE could push towards 4,200 before the year is out.
Yet major uncertainties remained over the outlook for 1997.
Signs that UK economic growth is gaining pace are expected to force Chancellor Kenneth Clarke to raise interest rates in the first quarter of the new year.
German shares charged ahead, breaking out of the narrow trading range of recent days, boosted by a sparkling performance overnight on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries.

The DAX index of 30 top German shares ended up 46.70 points, or 1.66 percent at 2,854.45. But in post-bourse computerised trading, the Ibis DAX was up just 10.71, or 0.38 percent, at 2835.54 having fallen back from the earlier highs in sympathy with other markets.
"We're having a party all around the world," said a trader.
French shares closed with a jump of more than one percent in heavy turnover, tracking the "Santa Claus rally" on Wall Street, traders said.

"The big push was today before people head for the hills," said a senior equity salesman, referring to departures for the Christmas week holiday. People also wanted to trade today as Monday marks the end of the December account.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.83 points or 1.33 percent at 2,278.53. The index was up 3.4 percent on the week.
Volume was a massive 13.05 billion francs.
The dollar trickled lower against the mark with the market winding down for the Christmas and New Year holiday season.
"We've seen nothing much today," one trader said. "It's very thin and the only orders are from people adjusting book positions. Christmas holidays seem to have started very early this year."
Despite its drift lower the dollar's bullish undertone remains intact and another strong performance on Wall Street helped limit the losses, traders said.
This Thursday's better-than-expected U.S. trade data and speculation of a rise in U.S. interest rates early next year should help the dollar end the year on a firm note, they added.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.5535 marks and 114.19 yen in late European trade, compared with 1.5597 marks and 114.07 yen business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 26.3 points higher at 4,077.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 29.83 at 2,278.53.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 46.70 at 2,854.45.
PRECIOUS MARKETS
Gold closed at $369.35 compared with Thursday's close of $369.05.
